title: The Hacker's Toolkit
description: A practical tour through ciphers that teach core cryptanalysis techniques — frequency analysis, pattern recognition, and algorithmic thinking.

stops.label: Caesar Cipher
stops.note: Try 25 nonidentity shifts (26 including the identity), then rank plaintext candidates.

stops.label: Monoalphabetic Sub.
stops.note: 26! possible alphabet permutations; language statistics can guide candidate searches but do not guarantee unique recovery.

stops.label: Homophonic Sub.
stops.note: Multiple symbols per letter can flatten frequencies; higher-order patterns may remain.

stops.label: Vigenère Cipher
stops.note: Kasiski and IC provide candidate periods, not a guaranteed key length.

stops.label: Playfair
stops.note: Digraph substitution — frequency analysis on letter pairs instead of singles.

stops.label: Columnar Transposition
stops.note: Anagramming columns — using frequency and contact analysis.

stops.label: Double Transposition
stops.note: Two differently keyed permutations complicate anagramming; compare period, message length and key reuse.

stops.label: Enigma
stops.note: Cribs, known-plaintext, and the Bombe — industrial-scale cryptanalysis.

stops.label: Codebreaker's Workbench
stops.note: Explore ciphertext with live analytical tools. Scores and candidates require interpretation; successful recovery is not guaranteed.
